items.label: Political dynasties in the province (Ateneo dataset)
items.detail: 22% of Zamboanga Sibugay's elected local positions were held by fat-dynastic officials after the 2025 election (16% in 2001); median province 28%; largest clan: Ruste (1.7% of positions); family poverty incidence 37% (2012).

items.label: Potential dynasts after the 2025 election (House CPBRD inventory)
items.detail: 36% of elected officials in the province have potential dynastic links (national average 54.5%; broader name matching than the Ateneo measure).

items.label: Political families in the province
items.detail: 0 of 1 elected officials in Zamboanga Sibugay (2025-2028) have a relative also in elective office (0%; national median 25%).

items.label: Weak: most of the winner's recent CPES evaluations are behind schedule
items.detail: Grace Construction Corporation: of 17 CPES evaluation(s) of its other DPWH contracts in the last 3 years, 9 (53%) were behind schedule. Worst, on 2024-06-28: 9.8% negative slippage during construction (CPES scored schedule 0.052 of 0.15) (contract 24KD0034).

items.label: Winner's other on-going roads
items.detail: Grace Construction Corporation has 3 on-going DPWH road(s) possibly stalled and 5 far behind schedule (weekly stage-3 list; DPWH progress data can lag).

items.label: CPES findings on another bidder's recent work
items.detail: Alraf Const. and Enterprises Inc.: of 2 CPES evaluation(s) of its other DPWH contracts in the last 3 years, 2 (100%) were behind schedule. Worst, on 2023-09-08: 7.2% negative slippage during construction (CPES scored schedule 0.078 of 0.15) (contract not stated).

assessment.derivation: 0 strong + 2 weak signal(s) → Medium priority (1 strong, or 2 weak) → Yellow.

sub: Budget, location, status, dates and bidders match this page.

steps.title: Open the bid documents
sub: Look for the quantities, a Bill of Quantities and technical specifications.

steps.title: Read Claude's check and confirm its points against the sources
Verify the risk: Procurement competition and bidding patterns
sub: Compare the bid-opening date with the Notice of Award date.
Ask whether post-qualification (checking the winner's documents and capacity) could be done that fast.

steps.title: Verify the risk: Implementation delays and performance anomalies
sub: Compare DPWH's reported progress with citizen reports, Bisto.ph inspections and satellite images.

If CPES is cited: open the DPWH quarterly CPES report for that date and confirm the contract, the slippage and the scores. A CPES rating is the agency's own evaluation; ask the district office for the evaluation sheet and the catch-up programme.

steps.title: Check site and field evidence
sub: Check progress on site: geotagged photos (from a monitor, a TPM civil-society partner or Bisto.ph), citizen reports on the DPWH portal, and DPWH's reported progress against the planned dates.

steps.title: Check the rule behind any threshold you are relying on
sub: Every threshold BantAI uses comes from a published rule. See Policies & Manuals for the procurement law, the slippage and termination circulars, the CPES guidelines and the field-monitoring manual.

steps.title: Write down what you found and keep the documents you relied on
sub: Screenshots, Bill of Quantities pages, photos or letters: attach them with your decision.

memo.subject: Request for review: DPWH road contract 26JF0001, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, ₱68.1 million
memo.rank: BantAI places it ranked 2 of 8 Yellow cases in Region IX on the current list
background: Fragmented procurement records and limited oversight capacity make it difficult to identify which Philippine road projects need closer scrutiny. The Commission on Audit's 2024 Annual Audit Report on the DPWH reported locally funded projects worth ₱138.23 billion that were not efficiently implemented: 1,435 finished late (₱77.4 billion), 523 suspended (₱33.6 billion), 491 carrying negative slippage of 10 per cent or more (₱19.2 billion), 114 not started (₱6.72 billion) and 33 terminated (₱1.29 billion) — 2,596 projects in all, most of them identified only after the money had been spent.

Project BantAI addresses this gap through AI-assisted risk screening that supports timely, targeted human review. It integrates public DPWH and PhilGEPS data and checks each contract against risk indicators that were tested on past project outcomes. A reviewer verifies the evidence before any case is referred, so that oversight offices can make informed decisions on which contracts to examine first.
memo.disclaimer: This is a request for review, not a finding of irregularity. BantAI ranks contracts by tested risk signs so that limited audit time can go to the contracts most worth a look. A sign is a reason to check, not evidence of wrongdoing, and several ordinary explanations may fit any of them.

signs.sign: Very fast award after bid opening
signs.found: Award made 7 days after the bid deadline (past road contracts awarded this fast had about twice the odds of termination)
signs.evidence: Termination odds ×2.1 (1.5–2.9); held on 2023–2025 (×2.6); ×3.7 on PhilGEPS data

signs.sign: Weak: most of the winner's recent CPES evaluations are behind schedule
signs.found: Grace Construction Corporation: of 17 CPES evaluation(s) of its other DPWH contracts in the last 3 years, 9 (53%) were behind schedule. Worst, on 2024-06-28: 9.8% negative slippage during construction (CPES scored schedule 0.052 of 0.15) (contract 24KD0034).
signs.evidence: The pattern across the winner's other contracts, over at least two evaluations: 0.51% of those contracts were terminated against 0.32%, odds ×1.57 (1.02–2.43). GPPB Circular 03-2019 requires a catch-up programme from 5% and a final warning from 10%

memo.basis: Two tested sign(s) appear together: 2 weak. Under BantAI's rules that makes the case Medium priority (Yellow). Each sign was tested against the outcomes of past road contracts before it was allowed to count towards the score; the odds for each are in the table above.
negatives: Price per km (₱54.0 million) is below the 95th percentile of comparable works (₱75.5 million, 424 contracts, Preventive maintenance / asphalt): within the normal range.
3 bidder(s) recorded. Bidder count is not a scored risk sign in our data, so it is not held against this contract.
No GPPB blacklist match and no [REVOKED] licence marker, checked by PCAB licence number.
No official action on record against a bidder, and no documented link between a bidder and an official.

No name match between the winner's PCAB Authorized Managing Officer and an elected official of the same area. Provincial political-family figures are shown on the case page as context only and are never scored.
